c.affects: who it affects: "all" (default), "allies" (you too), "other_allies" (not you), "enemies"; filters an area or aura, and a single target must match
c.aura: aura: sphere(radius=m). Passive: everyone inside who matches affects (you too) has this entry's bonuses while inside
c.auto_level: a fixed level instead of a roll (a formula), e.g. 2 for an automatic hard success
c.cast_time: cast time in minutes; under 1 is instant
c.check: the user's check (a check name); best("a", "b") rolls several and keeps the best; None / True always hits
c.difficulty: the user's difficulty (a formula; distance is available)
c.fixed_param: Fix a parameter: whenever this entry (or use) is used, the parameter has this value and isn't chosen. The value can be a formula. Closing a toggle use doesn't count parameters. Only this entry's parameters, not columns
c.guard: Guard (with an aura): those inside who match affects are guarded by you; enemy skills aimed at them (areas too) land on you
c.hit: hit condition (level, opp_level, opposed); None: success, and above the opponent when opposed
c.noise: noise radius in metres; None = silent
c.range: range in metres; None = unlimited; for a placement, how far from the user it may be put
c.reactions: if set the target may react: list checks and reaction skills (ID or name), or True for any reaction skill; players choose, NPCs get the best; a target who hasn't noticed the user can't react
c.requires: condition to use, e.g. not silenced
c.save: a save the target makes after a hit (a check name, against difficulty); saved in the script
c.seen_within: minutes within which you must have known where the target was (seen, told or located); None = not needed
c.target: single needs a target / self only / none
c.visible: the target must be perceived; a placement must be put within line of sight

config.hint:
One “name = value” per line tells the engine how this skill is used. Always prefix names in values: self. (you), target. (the target), this. (this entry). The common ones:
- target: who it is used on. "single" picks one, "self" only you, "none" nobody
- range: metres; leave out for unlimited
- cast_time: minutes to prepare; leave out for instant
- cooldown: minutes before it can be used again
- noise: metres within which others notice the use
- requires: when it can be used, e.g. self.mp >= 5
- check: the check to roll, e.g. "perception"
- reactions: how the target may respond, e.g. ["dodge"]
- shape: an area, e.g. sphere(radius=5) is a 5 m ball
config.short: One 'name = value' per line: who it targets, range, check, area, aura…

p.amount_dice: Amount: a formula, may roll dice, e.g. 2d6 + this.level

doc.placement: This skill places a trap or ward: it stays on the map and triggers when someone enters its radius

s.bonus: Always-on bonuses: the same code, always in effect. Only self., may use if and variables, no actions or with minutes; # note at line end; a line with only # note is for the KP
s.change: Change a value: = set, += add, -= subtract, *= multiply, /= divide. Runtime values (hp, mana, shield) change directly within their limits; attributes and derived values only for a while, inside with minutes(…):
s.minutes: Timed: the indented lines below wear off after N minutes. Attributes and derived values get a timed modifier; runtime values only += / -=, and what is left is taken back. No actions inside

shape.cone: A cone opening from the user toward a direction

verb.add: Old form; now write target.hp += 10 (timed: inside with minutes(…):). Adds to a runtime value, clamped to its limits
verb.damage: Take damage: shield first, then hp
verb.locate: Learn where they are right now (divination, scrying, a familiar's report): your side records a sighting, which seen_within skills use
verb.modify: Old form; now write inside with minutes(10):, e.g. target.str -= 2. Modifies a value for a while
verb.negate: As a reaction: void the attack on you (does nothing otherwise)
verb.set: Old form; now write self.hp = 0. Sets a runtime value, clamped to its limits
verb.sub: Old form; now write self.mp -= 5. Subtracts from a runtime value, clamped to its limits
verb.summon: Summon: put some characters of this template next to the receiver, controlled by the receiver's player; timed ones vanish. Add field=formula to fill their sheets
verb.teleport: Teleport next to another character (same spot, same building)

d.basic: Roll three six-sided dice and add them

fn.clamp: Keep x between lo and hi
fn.count: Count entries in a group: count(group) is how many, count(group.col, value) how many have that value in that column

fn.has: Whether this status is on you (1 or 0), e.g. has("rage")
fn.highest: Roll n dice with s sides, add the highest k
fn.inside: Whether you stand inside a placement you set with this entry (a circle or a whole building), e.g. inside("camp")
fn.lookup: Look a value up in one of the pack's tables
fn.lowest: Roll n dice with s sides, add the lowest k
fn.mod: Remainder of x / y (same sign as y)
fn.round: Round to nearest (.5 away from zero)
fn.sign: 1 if positive, -1 if negative, 0 if zero
fn.sum: Sum of one column over all entries of a group
fn.toggled: How many toggles are on in this group (toggle uses), e.g. toggled("gear")

fh.where: Dice work in a check's dice and in the keeper's ad-hoc checks and free rolls. Derived values, limits, initial values, targets and result conditions are recomputed every time, so they can't roll.

kp.chat_hint: Ask questions and clarify. The keeper answers only what your character could know; nothing here counts as an action.

params.by_kp_hint: Not chosen by the player: the KP sets it from the situation (e.g. how strong the local ley lines are)
params.check_hint: Rolled when chosen; on failure it counts as not chosen
params.cooldown_hint: How long before this entry can choose it again
params.defaults: When used you can also choose (parameters from the rule pack):
params.duration_hint: On a passive entry (no settings or script), its numbers (e.g. level) are multiplied for this long
params.hint: In formulas this.<name> is the number chosen this time.
params.item_own: This item's parameters (every use can pick them; optional)
params.label: Label
params.min_hint: The range when there are no choices (formulas)
params.multiplier_hint: When chosen, this use's damage, healing and added amounts are multiplied by it (costs are not); scripts see the total as boost
params.name: Name
params.own_hint: A parameter is a number chosen at use time, e.g. “burn lifespan: no=0, yes=1”. Choosing it can cost something or amplify the effect, or just carry a description for the KP.
params.requires_hint: Must hold to choose a non-zero value
params.script_hint: Runs whether or not the use lands, e.g. spend a resource elsewhere
params.spends_hint: Deducts the chosen number (e.g. how much mana to put in)

pdf.auto: Given by the rulebook from what is on the sheet

placement.hint: When set, the keeper places it on the map and these formulas give its values (they may use this.<column> and the owner's fields). Anyone walking into the radius triggers it once, as the engine works out from movement; the engine removes it when charges run out or it expires. Others spot it within their perception radius × the detection multiplier; the owner always sees it.
placement.is: This entry is a placed object (trap, ward…)

ph.perceive: e.g. 0.2 (smaller is harder to spot; 0 never)

play.map_hint: Tap a person or place to @ it; tap the ground to pick a destination. Describe height in words ("the rooftop", "100 m up").

react.hint: Pick one for each attack and send them together. The round waits for you.
react.title: You're under attack: choose how to react

review.leaks: Leak check hits (still present after one automatic rewrite):
review.not_in_review: This round is not awaiting review; read only.

rules.budget_columns: Columns counted (this column of every entry)
rules.budgets_hint: A cap on the sum of several values (e.g. 10 attribute points, 3 pluses), checked when characters are made. Negative values give points back; the cap may be a formula on the sheet; with no cap only the sum is shown.
rules.checks_hint: Each check is a bit of code (Edit opens it in the IDE on the right): dice, target, and the conditions for critical success / critical failure / success; otherwise it's a failure. The keeper decides who checks what against which difficulty (or opponent); the engine rolls. Skills whose settings name a check make it automatically.

cls_help.player: Player-defined: entered by the player during character creation.
cls_help.runtime: Runtime: changes during play (e.g. current HP); players can't set it, only the keeper's rulings change it. Needs an initial value.

rules.derived_hint: Numbers computed by formula from other fields; players can't enter them. The three below are required by the engine: keep their names, but write their formulas.
rules.editing: Editing {id} v{version}; saving creates a new version.

f.cls_group_hint: A column that changes in play: each entry keeps its own value, changed by self.set(this.col, …) in a script
f.gain_blocked: Can't be raised when (e.g. while healing is blocked)
f.label: Label
f.name: Name
f.param_check_hint: When set to non-zero the user must pass this check, or it counts as 0
f.param_cooldown_hint: After a non-zero value, how long before this entry can use it again (e.g. once a day: 1440)
f.vital: Vital: the character dies when it reaches 0

rules.fields_hint: Values and text on the sheet. The appearance field is required: other players' handles for this character are generated from it.
rules.formulas_hint: Formulas with a name that can be used anywhere, e.g. dex_bonus.

g.damage_kind_hint: The type of damage that entries in this group (rule-written or player-written) deal in their scripts. The one hurt applies their template's damage-taken formula, e.g. set magic here and anti-magic applies.
g.effects: Entries may carry modifiers and a skill script
g.fields: Header: columns every entry fills besides name and description
g.fields_hint: Think of a group as a table: each row is an entry (one skill) and already has Name and Description columns. Add extra columns here, e.g. rank (number), mana cost (number), damage (dice formula). Fixed entries below and players' own entries fill in these columns. Leave empty if you need none.
g.hidden: Hide the whole group from players
g.label: Group name (shown to players)
g.name: Group ID (internal code)
g.placements: Entries may be placed objects (traps, wards… left on the map)
g.presets: Fixed entries: rows filled in by the rules
g.presets_hint: Rows filled in from the header above, so players don't write them; entries players write are extra rows. When the condition is true the entry appears on the sheet and its effects apply; otherwise it doesn't appear. Conditions may only use this sheet's fields; text values need quotes, e.g. class == "warrior", class != "warrior" or class == "warrior" and str >= 3. Fixed entries don't count toward the min/max above.
g.reactions: Entries can be reactions (used when attacked; instant ones only)
g.reveal_hint: Whether those who notice the use and can see the user learn what was used (a condition; this.<column> works, including numbers filled in for this use; empty = yes). Set by the rule pack; players cannot change it. The fields ticked below are revealed along with it, e.g. calling out the name gives away who you are.
g.settings: More settings: switches and area shapes
g.shapes: Area shapes entries may have (for area attacks, beams…; leave all unticked if unused)
g.timing: Entries have a casting time and a cooldown (skills)
g.uses: Items: an entry is used only through its uses

rules.groups_hint: A group is one kind of entry on the sheet, such as class skills, personal skills or special abilities; make one group per kind. Each entry under it is one specific skill or ability. Entries come from two places: players add their own when creating a character, and you can write fixed entries here (optionally with a condition, e.g. only for one class).

gt.empty: No entries yet. Use “+ Row” below.
gt.hint: This kind of entry is a table: each row is an entry written by the rules (e.g. one skill), each column is something every entry fills in. Condition, Name and Description come with every row; “+ Column” adds one (e.g. rank, mana cost, damage), and clicking a column name edits its name and type. The “Script” button opens the entry's skill script in the IDE on the right; the ⤢ next to a formula cell opens it there too. Modifiers and area shapes are under the row's “More”. Conditions may only use this sheet's fields, e.g. class == "warrior"; empty means always. Row order matters: modifiers on one value run top to bottom. Players fill the same columns for their own entries.
gt.id_hint: English ID, needed to refer to this entry in formulas: hero.fireball is whether it exists (1 or 0), hero.fireball.level is its level column. Must be unique on a sheet.
gt.player_fills: Empty: the player fills it in
gt.player_fills_hint: A column left empty on a fixed entry is filled in by each player when making the character (e.g. each one's own level). If the column is required, it must be filled whenever the entry applies.
gt.script_bad: The skill script has problems; click to see
gt.script_empty: No skill script yet; click to write one in the IDE
gt.script_ok: Open the skill script in the IDE
gt.timing_hint: Cast time and cooldown are in minutes and may be formulas (24*60 is a day). Under 1 minute is instant; an action using the skill takes at least the cast time. Cooldown: after a use (hit or not) the skill can't be used again for this long.
gt.title: Entry table

rules.handbook_hint: The full rules for players (Markdown: # headings, - lists, | tables |). The site shows it as its own page and the KP reads it too. Write [[heading]] in any description in the pack and the character form expands that section of the rulebook in place.

help.appearance: Appearance: the player describes how the character looks. When others first see the character, its handle (e.g. "woman in a red scarf") is generated from this. It can't be removed or retyped.
help.can_fly: Can fly: ticked by the player, off by default. Flyers travel in a straight line at fly speed; others go up or down first and then along the ground at move speed. It can't be removed or retyped.
help.concealment: Multiplies how far others can notice this character: 1 is normal, 0.3 means others must be much closer. The default 1 is fine.
help.fly_multiplier: How many times the move speed a flyer flies. Default 1. Only matters for characters who can fly.
help.fly_speed: Metres per minute when flying; default fly_multiplier * move_speed. Only matters for characters who can fly.
help.hear_distance: How far (in metres) this character hears people talking. Bystanders within this range of either speaker hear the whole conversation, relayed by the keeper. Required, e.g. 30 * hear_multiplier. Walls are ignored.
help.hear_multiplier: Hearing multiplier, default 1. Skills and statuses can modify it (e.g. keen ears ×2); use it in the hearing range formula.
help.hp: HP: every kind of character must have it, as a runtime value. Its limits, initial value and change per minute can be edited; its name, kind and class can't. Damage comes off shield first (if there is one), then HP.
help.move_speed: Metres per minute. Required, e.g. 80 for an ordinary person, or 60 + agi * 2.
help.perception_radius: How far (in metres) this character notices others. Required, e.g. 50 + per, or a constant like 100.

ins.groups: Learns the entries in the subject's groups:
ins.when_hint: Worked out on the observer; target.<name> reads the subject; empty = always

rules.insights_hint: When an observer sees (or senses) a subject, the engine tells the observer's player these things from the subject's sheet and records them as intel; it tells again when a value changes. Everything else is judged by the KP from what players see, hear and find out, a little at a time.

kind_help.boolean: Yes/no: a checkbox, e.g. can fly. It's 1 or 0 in formulas.
kind_help.formula: Dice formula: a formula that may roll dice, e.g. a skill's damage 1d str, or dice(this.level, lookup(table, this.level)). In a group each entry fills its own and may use this.<column>. In the skill script and this entry's other formulas, this.<that column> uses the formula (rolled then), e.g. the script target.damage(this.damage).
kind_help.param: Chosen on use: a number the player picks each time the skill is used, e.g. how much mana to spend. Not filled at character creation; the player says it in the action and the keeper passes it to the engine when rolling. Min and max are formulas that may use the character's fields and this.<column>. With a resource to spend from, the engine checks there is enough and deducts it when the round resolves. Dice formulas refer to it as this.<column name>, e.g. (1d4 + int) * floor(30 / this.mp_spent).
kind_help.resource: Resource: a value that gets spent or restored (HP, mana, shield, uses left). The maximum may be a formula such as hp_max; empty means no limit.
kind_help.text: Text: descriptions such as background; with choices, the player picks one of them.

rules.levels_hint: Checked in order; the first true condition wins. Variables: roll, target, difficulty, opp_roll, opp_target.
rules.locked: Required by the engine; can't be changed
rules.order_matters_presets: Note: the order of fixed entries matters; effects on the same value run top to bottom.

p.what: One row of the table, i.e. one concrete entry (e.g. one skill). Name and description come with every row; each box further down is one column you added in the header above.

rules.params_hint: Numbers chosen at use time (e.g. “use +”, “how much mana”): tick the groups each applies to. Players can add their own on entries and uses; what can be chosen is both together.

ph.budget_desc: a line for the player making the character
ph.choices: e.g. red, blue, green (comma-separated; leave empty for free text)
ph.choices_number: e.g. E=1, D=2, C=3, B=4, A=5, EX=10, or 1~5, 10 (empty for any number)
ph.choices_param: e.g. no=0, yes=1; one of these is chosen on use, the first if not said
ph.damage_taken: e.g. max(0, amount - 5 * anti_magic) if kind == "magic" else amount; empty = take it as is
ph.gain_blocked: empty means never, e.g. hp_heal_blocked > 0: while true, skill scripts can only lower it
ph.max_resource: e.g. hp_max; empty means no limit
ph.per_minute: empty means none, e.g. 1 or con / 2
ph.search: e.g. 1d20 + per; empty = can't find hidden ones
ph.stealth: e.g. 10 + 5 * ceil(distance / 40) if distance <= 200 else 999; empty = never hides
ph.table_rows:
One per line: key,value
e.g. warrior,14

rules.pick: Choose a rule pack and version…
rules.player_entities: Entities each player creates (template, min, max)
rules.player_entities_hint: Which kinds of character each player creates, and how many of each.
rules.problems: {n} problems; can't save a version yet (drafts are always fine)
rules.rules_text: Rules text (free text for the keeper)
rules.rules_text_hint: Rules text for the keeper: everything the pack can't express as formulas.
rules.samples_hint: Checked on save: every example must produce the expected derived values.

t.damage_taken_hint: Each time a character of this template takes skill damage, the engine uses this to work out how much (never below 0). amount is the raw damage, kind its type (from the skill's group, or damage(amount, "type")). Resistances written here apply to every attack.
t.description_hint: Shown at the top of this part of the character form; write [[heading]] to cite a rulebook section
t.label: Shown to players as
t.name: Template ID
t.name_label_hint: Title and hint of the name box on the character page, e.g. 'What you call them'; empty uses the default
t.on_death_hint: Runs the moment a character of this template dies (same syntax as skill scripts). self is the dead one, target whoever hurt it last, partners by template name (e.g. companion.set(fading, 1)).
t.stealth_hint: Stealth is worked out on this character: what someone distance metres away must roll to notice it (observer.<name> reads the observer's sheet); 0 means not hiding. Search is the roll this character makes to notice others. At the start of each round every observer that can see a hider it hasn't found rolls once; once found it stays found until out of sight. Using a skill on someone reveals you to them; a target that hasn't noticed its attacker can't react.

table.bad_rows: Line {lines} can't be read and isn't saved: write key,value with a number value

rules.tables_hint: One row per line: key,value. Range tables take the largest key not above the input; exact tables need an exact match.
rules.template_hint: A template is the format of one kind of character sheet, not a specific character: players fill a sheet from it. One template is enough if every player has the same kind of sheet; add a second if each player also controls, say, a companion. The ID is an internal code (lowercase letters, digits, underscores, e.g. hero); the label is what players see. The default character works as is.
rules.unsaved: Unsaved changes; a draft is saved automatically

uses.description: What this use does (with no config or script, the KP rules on it from this text)
uses.hint: An entry can be used in several ways (e.g. a weapon swung normally, or unleashed); each use is a skill, named “entry/use”. A use's config falls back to the entry's; this.<column> in its script is the entry's column.
uses.kp_rules: Ruled by the KP from the text
uses.name: Use name
uses.templates_hint: Use templates: players adding uses to their own entries can copy one of these (e.g. a standard area blast) and adjust it.
uses.title: Uses

wb.fix_first: Fix the problems before saving a version (drafts can always be saved)

script.hint: When the skill takes effect the engine runs it line by line. Always write a prefix: self., target., this. Change values with = += -= *= /=, actions are functions, timed changes go in with minutes(…):.
script.ph:
e.g.
target.damage(this.damage)
self.mp -= this.mp_spent
with minutes(10):
    target.move_speed *= 0.5
script.short: Runs line by line. Change values: target.hp -= 10, self.mp -= this.mp_spent; actions: target.damage(2d6); timed changes go in with minutes(10):.
script.title: Skill script (on use)

state.patch_hint: Edits are validated like adjudications and logged as admin overrides.

talk.hint: Talking happens face to face and is heard at once. While any conversation is open the round won't resolve; talking takes no game time.
talk.invited_me: @{label} wants to talk to you. If you accept, what you were doing stops and you'll act again after the talk.
talk.none: No conversation. Use Talk next to someone in the map tab's “Currently perceived” list.

uses.toggle_hint: Each use flips it on or off; its modifiers apply while on
